title: Wildfire-smoke health red flags
summary: Recognise when smoke exposure requires urgent movement to cleaner air and professional help, especially for vulnerable people.
content: Working sequence: Escalate for severe breathing difficulty, chest symptoms, confusion, fainting, blue or grey colour, inability to speak normally, or rapidly worsening established disease. Make the scene safe, use consent where possible, and call emergency services for immediate threats for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Observe breathing, alertness, major bleeding, severe pain, temperature exposure, and rapid change without inventing a diagnosis for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Give only low-risk care within training and follow the person’s established professional plan for medicines or chronic needs for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Record time, observations, actions, medicines already taken, allergies, response, and who was contacted for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Reassess frequently and arrange qualified help early when danger signs, uncertainty, or deterioration are present for “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Do not diagnose, prescribe, improvise dosing, perform invasive procedures, or delay emergency help in “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”. Protect privacy and infection-control boundaries, but never let paperwork delay lifesaving action in “Wildfire-smoke health red flags”.
